personas.background: Semi-retired IT consultant. Has lived on Maple Street for eight years and considers himself the de facto organiser — starts most threads, chases replies, books the village hall. Slightly over-involved. Means well.

activities.value: strongly prefers settling disputes internally on the street before contacting the council

social.value: enjoys running neighbourhood events; takes organiser role seriously

preference_history.old_value: moderate involvement; attended most events without leading
preference_history.new_value: now organises nearly everything; became de facto chair after the previous organiser moved away in session 2
preference_history.trigger: previous street organiser (Len) moved away; no one else stepped up so Femi took over permanently

speaking_quirks: always opens threads with 'Quick question for the street'
uses 'just checking' as a softener before opinions

personas.background: Retired school librarian. Has lived on Maple Street for 30 years. The street's institutional memory. Deeply opposed to any development that changes the street's character — new builds, conversions, additional parking. Warmly social but immovable on planning matters.

activities.value: opposes any planning application that would change the street's residential character — new builds, loft conversions, additional hardstanding

social.value: attends every street event; values the social fabric of the street above practical concerns

domain_specific.value: drives and relies on the unmanaged parking; would be disadvantaged by a residents' parking scheme that charges

preference_history.old_value: would contact the council directly if something bothered her
preference_history.new_value: now raises everything in the group chat first after being persuaded by Femi that collective action works better
preference_history.trigger: Femi showed her that a joint objection to a planning application carried more weight than an individual letter

speaking_quirks: references 'thirty years on this street' when defending a position
calls every positive change 'progress for the wrong reasons'
uses 'I remember when' to introduce historical comparisons

personas.background: Graphic designer. Rents a flat at no. 14. Has lived there for just over a year. Uses the group chat for practical things — lost parcels, bin day queries — and enjoys the community spirit without getting drawn into politics. Aware that as a renter they have less stake in planning disputes.

activities.value: stays neutral on planning and development debates; notes they are a renter and have less at stake

social.value: enjoys street social events; attends if they are not too formal

domain_specific.value: does not have a car; indifferent to parking schemes either way

preference_history.old_value: lurked mostly; posted only for practical queries in first months
preference_history.new_value: started engaging socially after meeting neighbours at the session 2 street party
preference_history.trigger: attended the street party in session 2; met Claudette and Femi in person and felt part of the community

speaking_quirks: prefaces opinions with 'not sure if this is my place but...'
adds thumbs-up reactions rather than full replies when agreeing

personas.background: GP. Bought her house twelve years ago. Uses the group chat minimally — reads everything, replies rarely, but when she does it is direct and final. Has strong views about noise (she works early) and parking (she does home visits). Bypasses the group chat when she has a serious complaint and goes straight to the council.

activities.value: prefers to contact the council directly rather than coordinating through the group chat

social.value: skips most street social events due to early starts; attends the December one as a matter of courtesy

domain_specific.value: supports a residents' parking scheme; needs guaranteed parking near her house for home visits

preference_history.new_value: started reporting noise directly to the council after sleep disruption affected her work performance; does not mention it in the group chat
preference_history.trigger: was called in for an early emergency after a bad night due to street noise; decided she would not tolerate it further

speaking_quirks: sends short factual updates with no commentary: 'Bin collection moved to Thursday this week.'
uses 'For the avoidance of doubt' before correcting something
never uses emoji or exclamation marks

personas.background: Stay-at-home parent, two children aged 5 and 7. Has lived on the street for five years. The most active poster — knows everyone through the school run and playground. Uses the chat partly for practical updates and partly to keep an eye on things. Worries about traffic and child safety more than anything else.

activities.value: prioritises child safety on the street above all other concerns — traffic, speeding, parking on pavements

social.value: attends and helps at street events; brings kids

domain_specific.value: supports a residents' parking scheme specifically because it would reduce pavement parking near the school gate

preference_history.old_value: mentioned traffic as a concern occasionally
preference_history.new_value: became vocal advocate for traffic calming after near-miss involving his older child at the school gate in session 3
preference_history.trigger: his child nearly stepped into a car reversing off a driveway at the school gate; he posted immediately and now raises traffic safety in almost every relevant thread

speaking_quirks: mentions the school gate in almost every safety discussion
uses 'as a parent' before safety-related points
follows up every unresolved thread to ask if anything has been decided

edges.history_summary: Femi relies on Claudette's institutional knowledge; Claudette has adopted Femi's preference for collective action over individual council letters.
Femi introduced Jordan to the group chat and checks in on them occasionally.
shared_events: met at the session 2 street party

edges.history_summary: Femi wants group consensus; Vera goes straight to the council. They are cordial but represent opposite approaches.
Both invest heavily in the street's community life. Marcus helps Femi organise events; Femi amplifies Marcus's safety concerns.
Claudette has taken a quiet liking to Jordan after meeting them at the street party. Jordan finds Claudette's local history charming.
shared_events: talked at the street party for an hour about the street's history

edges.history_summary: They have coexisted for twelve years. Claudette finds Vera brusque; Vera finds Claudette's planning opposition occasionally useful.
Claudette adores Marcus's children. Marcus listens respectfully to her history of the street.
shared_events: Marcus's children trick-or-treated at Claudette's for three years running

edges.history_summary: Have barely interacted. Vera barely uses the chat; Jordan doesn't knock on doors.
Jordan occasionally helps Marcus with the school run in a pinch. They wave in the morning.
Both care about parking but for different reasons. They have aligned on the residents' scheme without discussing it directly.

group_norms.norm_text: Post to the chat before calling the council — we sort things on the street first.
Reply if you're coming to street events — silence means no.
No posting to the chat after 10pm.
